slots.practicalActivity: Using Brightfield Industrial Group's Phase 1 scope (GL, AP, AR, and Cash Management for US operations only, with Fixed Assets and Canada deferred), draft a one-page roster assigning the Executive Sponsor, client-side Project Manager, Business Process Owners, partner-side Project Manager, Solution Architect, Functional Consultants, Technical Consultants, Data Migration Lead, Testing Lead, and OCM Lead to Brightfield's actual team. Then sketch a one-page Work Breakdown Structure with one workstream per module plus technical, data migration, testing, and OCM workstreams, and open a 3-entry RAID log that includes the real risk from the lesson: the legacy export tool untested against the new chart of accounts.
slots.deliverable: A one-page Brightfield project team roster, a WBS outline with named workstreams, and a 3-entry RAID log.

slots.practicalActivity: Write out Brightfield's business requirement BR-CM-014 ("Treasury needs same-day visibility into cash positions across all US bank accounts") and translate it into a functional requirement the way a Functional Consultant would. Then plan a one-hour requirements workshop for Cash Management: list the agenda items, the facilitator and scribe roles, at least two objectives, and one parking-lot entry capturing Brightfield's manual, spreadsheet-based wire-matching problem exactly as it surfaces in the lesson.
slots.deliverable: A completed business-requirement-to-functional-requirement translation plus a one-page workshop agenda with a parking-lot entry.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending practice for Implementation Methodology: build a Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM) template with columns for Requirement ID, description, owner, priority, status, design decision, configuration/extension, and test script. Populate it with 5 realistic Brightfield Cash Management requirements (same-day cash visibility, automated wire matching, the foreign-currency wire edge case, Treasury's legacy report format, and new bank account setup) so every later chapter in this course can trace back to it.
slots.deliverable: A 5-row Requirements Traceability Matrix for Brightfield Cash Management, ready to be referenced through fit-gap, configuration, and testing.

slots.practicalActivity: Run a mock fit-gap session against the 5-row RTM from the previous slot: classify each requirement as Fit, Configuration gap, Process gap, or Extension gap, the way the lesson classifies Brightfield's wire-matching problem as mostly a configuration gap with one extension gap. Then write a full gap/solution log entry, modeled directly on GAP-CM-03, for the legacy Treasury report requirement: Gap ID, description, business impact, gap type, proposed solution, effort estimate, priority, owner, and status.
slots.deliverable: A 5-row classified fit-gap table plus one fully-written gap/solution log entry with all nine required fields.

lessons.title: Business Process Design and Solution Design Documents

slots.practicalActivity: Draft one configuration workbook row for Brightfield's "Manage Reconciliation Matching Rules" task list: setup object name, every attribute needing a value, the proposed values, the related gap ID, and a sign-off column, mirroring the wire-transfer auto-match row from the lesson. Lock in an enterprise structure decision for Brightfield's Phase 1 (legal entities, business units, the ledger's 4 Cs, and reference data sets). Then outline a one-page Business Process Design narrating the future-state cash reconciliation process end to end, from statement import through the custom Treasury report.
slots.deliverable: One configuration workbook row, one written enterprise structure decision, and a one-page Business Process Design outline.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending practice for Analysis and Design: assemble the Design-phase sign-off package for Brightfield's Cash Management module by combining the fit-gap results, the gap/solution log entry, the configuration workbook row, and the enterprise structure decision into a Solution Design Document (SDD) section. Specify exactly how the auto-match rule is configured (tolerances, transaction types) and the technical build for the custom BI Publisher Treasury report (data model, layout, scheduling), ready for Business Process Owner and Solution Architect sign-off.
slots.deliverable: A one-to-two-page Solution Design Document section that would pass the Design-phase gate into Configure.

lessons.title: Setup and Maintenance and Implementation Projects

slots.practicalActivity: Scope an Implementation Project named "Brightfield Phase 1 — Financials" by listing the Functional Setup Manager task lists under the Cash Management functional area that belong in it (including "Define Banks, Branches, and Accounts" and "Manage Reconciliation Matching Rules"). Then write a configuration-package promotion plan for moving that setup from the development environment to Test: what travels automatically in the package, what has to be set manually in each environment (the bank-statement integration endpoint), and the comparison-report check you'd run before import.
slots.deliverable: A task-list scoping list for the Implementation Project, plus a promotion plan naming at least one environment-specific exception.

slots.practicalActivity: Build Brightfield's Cash Management data migration scope: sort its legacy data into static/reference, open balances, and historical categories, and state which loading mechanism (FBDI, ADFdi, manual entry, or REST API) applies to each. Note how Brightfield's update-cohort calendar shapes when its cutover rehearsal gets scheduled. Then write one cleansing rule for the dash-formatted bank account numbers the lesson describes, and one validation check (count and dollar total of open unreconciled items vs. an independent legacy report) a mock load would have to pass.
slots.deliverable: A one-page data migration scope table plus one cleansing rule and one validation check, grounded in the Brightfield Cash Management conversion.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for Configuration and Migration: write a full mock-conversion runbook for Brightfield's Cash Management data, in order — static/reference data loaded first via FBDI, then open balances loaded shortly before go-live. Name the two cleansing fixes the first mock load would surface (the account-number dash format), and write the exact reconciliation check the Treasury Manager would have to sign off before the team proceeds toward the real cutover load.
slots.deliverable: A mock-load runbook with a load order, one cleansing fix, and a sign-off reconciliation check.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a one-page test plan scope statement (scope, levels, environments, roles, entry/exit criteria) for Brightfield's Cash Management testing. Then write test script CM-TS-07 in full — numbered steps, expected result, and pass/fail outcome — for the same-day cash visibility requirement (BR-CM-014), and add a second script covering the partial-payment reconciliation scenario that fails during SIT in the lesson.
slots.deliverable: A one-page test plan plus two complete, numbered test scripts each traced to a real requirement ID.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a UAT scenario for the Treasury Manager that retests the partial-payment fix and adds the foreign-currency wire scenario the SIT script never covered. Log the resulting defect as DEF-CM-04, with ID, description, steps to reproduce, severity, priority, owner, and status, and move it through the full life cycle from New to Closed. Then build a 5-script regression test suite (including a re-run of CM-TS-07) to run every quarter inside the Test-to-Production update window.
slots.deliverable: One UAT scenario script, one fully worked defect-log entry moved to Closed, and a 5-item regression test suite list.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for Testing: run a full SIT-to-UAT-to-sign-off simulation for Brightfield Cash Management. Execute test script CM-TS-07 and the partial-payment script on paper, log any failure as a defect and move it through triage to Closed, then write the formal UAT sign-off statement a Business Process Owner would actually sign — the exit criterion that closes TCM's Validate phase.
slots.deliverable: A worked SIT/UAT execution log with at least one logged-and-closed defect, plus a signed UAT sign-off statement.

slots.practicalActivity: Write Brightfield's cutover runbook hour by hour: the Friday 5 PM legacy freeze, the overnight extract, the Saturday-morning load, at least two validation checkpoints with named go/no-go decisions, a rollback plan, and a communication plan. Then write the steering committee's go-live decision memo, citing the specific validation evidence from the lesson (trial balance tie-out, open AP/AR load confirmation, reconciliation data match) that justified the Monday go-live.
slots.deliverable: An hour-by-hour cutover runbook plus a one-paragraph go/no-go decision memo citing specific validation evidence.

slots.practicalActivity: Design Brightfield's four-week hypercare plan: staffing, stand-up cadence (daily tapering to three times a week), and exit criteria tied to completing a full month-end close. Define the Tier 1/Tier 2/Tier 3 steady-state support model it hands off to, and write one Oracle Service Request at the correct severity (Severity 3) for the Cash Management rounding-discrepancy scenario. Then outline a role-based training plan — train-the-trainer for AP/Treasury super users plus a shadow/reverse-shadow knowledge-transfer schedule for the two internal Tier 2 staff.
slots.deliverable: A hypercare plan with exit criteria, a tiered support model, one correctly-severitied Service Request, and a training/knowledge-transfer schedule.

slots.practicalActivity: Course capstone review: produce a single, ordered "implementation playbook" for Brightfield Industrial Group's Cash Management module that chains every artifact built across this course — the RTM, the fit-gap classification table, the gap/solution log entry, the configuration workbook row, the enterprise structure decision, the Business Process Design and Solution Design Document, the data migration scope and mock-load runbook, the test plan and scripts, the defect log, the UAT sign-off, the cutover runbook, the go-live decision memo, and the hypercare/support handoff — into one reference document a new Functional Consultant could follow start to finish.
slots.deliverable: One consolidated implementation playbook document linking every prior artifact in lifecycle order, from requirements through hypercare.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can function on a real Oracle Fusion Financials implementation team: translate business requirements into a signed-off fit-gap analysis and configuration workbook, write and run test scripts through SIT and UAT, and plan a cutover through go-live and hypercare into steady-state production support.
